title: Beyond End-to-End: Understanding the Limits of LLMs in Scientific Problem Solving
problem: Existing multimodal LLM (MLLM) benchmarks for scientific question answering are end-to-end only, making it difficult to identify where and why models fail. Models fail on high-resolution visual data without scripting or tool use.
motivation: Develop fine-grained evaluation frameworks to expose reasoning bottlenecks in MLLMs and understand integration failures across subtasks, motivating agent-based or multi-model approaches.
method: Instead of just testing whether models get scientific questions right or wrong, the researchers broke down the task into smaller steps—like identifying coordinates on an image or calculating exact pixel locations—to see exactly where models fail. They evaluated two multimodal language models, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct, on high-resolution visual data using this decomposed approach.
key_novelty: Breaking scientific question-answering into small subtasks shows where multimodal language models—AI systems that interpret images and text—get stuck in their reasoning or fail to integrate their components properly.
contributions: Evaluation framework decomposing scientific QA into subtasks for fine-grained assessment
Analysis of two state-of-the-art MLLMs on high-resolution visual data
Identification of reasoning integration failures despite individual task competence
Evidence that agent-based or multi-model approaches needed for complex tasks

metrics.primary: End-to-end reasoning accuracy and integration failures
metrics.secondary: Per-subtask accuracy on coordinate mapping and pixel computation

limitations: Study limited to two MLLM models; no comparison with multi-model or agent-based approaches mentioned
primary_theme: MLLM Reasoning Bottlenecks in Scientific Tasks
